newsitem.title: INDIA: India CRISIL gives 'AA (so)' rating for Bharat PTC.
newsitem.headline: India CRISIL gives 'AA (so)' rating for Bharat PTC.

text.p: India's Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) said on Wednesday it has assigned a "AA (so)" rating to its 56.5 million rupees securitisation programme of Bharat Forge Ltd (BFL).
This indicates high safety regarding timely payment of obligations on the instrument, it said in a statement.

The rating is based on the originator's (BFL's) collection and follow-up mechanisms, the pool selection criteria, the credit enhancement provided to the transaction, the warranties provided by BFL and the integrity of the legal structure.

The 56.5 million rupees Pass-Through-Certificates (PTCs) are backed by hire purchase receivables from 283 identified car loans. The first and last pay-outs are January 1997 and June 1999 respectively. These loans have been originated by the Lease & Hire Purchase division of BFL, whose activities consist of hire purchase and lease financing of plant & machinery, cars and commercial vehicles, CRISIL said.

It said that BFL is the flagship company of the Kalyani group, engaged primarily in the manufacturing of heavy forgings. The company has outstanding ratings of AA for non-convertible debentures, FAA+ for fixed deposits and P1+ for short term debt. BFL's financial services activities, commenced in 1992/93, encompass bill discounting, ICD lending, hire-purchase and leasing.

BFL's overall month-on-month collection efficiency on its car portfolio (new cars) has been 76.3 percent. While collections from current dues have been fairly high and steady, collections from overdues have been relatively poor.

CRISIL said taking into account the portfolio performance and the relatively limited track record of the originator, a credit-cum-liquidity enhancement of 8.475 million rupees, or 15 percent of the future receivables on the pool at the point of securitisation, has been stipulated for the securitisation programme. Out of this, three million rupees is the liquidity enhancement required to be set aside upfront in a bank account, which will be available to meet any shortfall in collections on the pool and will always be topped up to this level in case of a draw down. The remaining 5,475 million rupees are in the form of Bank Guarantee.

BFL is the Originator of the receivables and the Issuer of the Pass-Through-Certificates. The company will assign the receivables to the investor in the PTCs by paying stamp duty. The initial investor will act as the Agent & Trustee to the transaction and will operate the cash collateral account. The transaction is bankruptcy remote as regards BFL. Amongst other things, BFL will warranty to keep the documentation perfect, to follow-up on collections on the securitised contracts with due diligence, to keep the assets unencumbered and insured etc.
The statement also said that, BFL has only a limited track record in the automobile financing business.
